note: Read off Ion's reference sheet. He is painted BY PART rather than by
garment — see LIMBS in paint-skinned.js — because a machine is not
wearing anything and 'where does the sleeve end' is not a question he
has an answer to. Which colour a piece of him is IS which piece it is,
and the rig already knows that.
Every number is a fraction of the figure: yN is height with 0 at the
sole and 1 at the crown, ax is |x| over the fingertip reach, zN is
depth over height, all read in the T-pose.
The drawing and the mesh agree closely. Drawn neck 0.662-0.697 against
a rig that puts it at 0.662-0.720; drawn head bottom 0.697 against
0.677. What the mesh said: foot 0.000-0.108, leg 0.076-0.422, hips
0.662-0.720, head 0.677-1.000 — a third of him is head.
The eyes were MEASURED, not placed. They are modelled — two discs and a
mouth bar standing a hair proud of a recessed panel — but only a hair:
the whole screen sits between zN 0.165 and 0.190, so depth cannot tell
them from the panel. Taking the frontmost group and clustering it by
SIGNED x finds them exactly: left at x -0.177 r 0.047, right at x 0.190
r 0.045, both at y 0.808 r 0.026. Their radii come out at 0.565 of the
width, against the 0.536 a truly round disc would give at this scale,
which is how we know they are discs and not ovals.
NOT PAINTED: the salmon rings on the head bolts, the shoulder and the
knees, and the mouth bar under the eyes — the rings are geometry no
height can find, and the mouth is three vertices across.
